task.title: Page finite recurrence occurrences through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/873 by composing exact recurrence replay with bounded occurrence paging in one read-only command.
acceptance_criteria: Validate recurrence identity and page size before storage access, then load only the selected recurrence stream.
Emit ordered compact occurrence JSON with exact provenance and the first unreturned authored offset or null.
Preserve categorized failures and grant no persisted cursor, due, catch-up, materialization, claim, dispatch, retry, or execution authority.

attempts.diagnostic: Focused CLI integration tests failed because recurrence occurrences was not recognized.
attempts.patch: Added paging, final-page, invalid identity and size, out-of-range, missing and corrupt storage, exact-stream isolation, output, and non-mutation tests.

attempts.summary: Implemented the minimal read-only paging composition.
attempts.diagnostic: The kernel already owned exact replay and bounded arithmetic, so duplicating either in the CLI would weaken a tested boundary.
attempts.patch: Composed RecurrenceStore::load with occurrences_page, reused borrowed JSON projection, added stable diagnostics and ADR-0044.

attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit identified duplicated exact-load flow and a future non-exhaustive lookup-error taxonomy that could be misclassified.
attempts.patch: Centralized exact recurrence loading, preserved out-of-range versus infrastructure failures, reran pinned verification, and merged after CodeRabbit covered 38410d1 through exact head 294ec1f with no actionable comments.

outcome.summary: The CLI pages one exact durable finite recurrence in stable order through existing read-only kernel contracts and deterministic diagnostics.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0170-recurrence-occurrence-paging-cli.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 171 records: 171 valid, 0 invalid

lessons: Compose exact load and bounded projection rather than scanning inventory or duplicating arithmetic.
Keep domain out-of-range failures distinct from storage and future infrastructure failures.

CodeRabbit found duplicated exact-load flow and a non-exhaustive error-taxonomy risk; loading was centralized and out-of-range errors remained distinct from infrastructure failures before substantive re-review.
A continuation offset in output remains inert caller-owned projection state.
Review-fix commits require their own substantive incremental coverage.
